- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) or shows sharp drops, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast increase to 3% max after spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has moved >3% from 10-day average, model often overshoots — adjust forecast toward prior 10-day mean.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to underestimate late-period (last 10 days) price movements — add 0.5–1.5% buffer for final 10 days if sentiment is rising.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.8), model misreads momentum — use weighted average of sentiment peaks and troughs for smoothing.
